item.title: Greece is the most popular luxury honeymoon destination for 2027 – with Italy and France also in the top 10
item.description: Greece tops the ranking of the world’s most popular honeymoon destinations for 2027 in Virtuoso’s latest Luxe Report, ahead of Bali and the Maldives.

item.title: Jurist Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize for 2026
item.description: Announcing the award, Jørgen Watne Frydnes, the chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee, said the award was going to a "person who with exceptional courage and integrity has led the way towards a more comprehensive global legal order."

item.title: Violence is 'not general' in French students protests, MEP says
item.description: French S&D MEP Emma Rafowicz says Emmanuel Macron’s government is “completely irresponsible” in its handling of the ongoing student protests in France.

item.title: Scientific study reveals scariest horror movie – with one 2026 title breaking heart rate record
item.description: The ranking was determined by a study monitoring audience's heart rates and BPM increases while watching horror films.

item.title: Former New Zealand PM: Associate membership with Brussels "very interesting" for the country
item.description: Helen Clark, former prime minister of New Zealand, says a form of associate membership of the European Union, similar to the proposal for Canada, would be “very interesting”. She highlights access to the single market as a potential key benefit for a “distant trading country” such as New Zealand.

item.title: Police arrest suspect after deadly shooting in Germany's Upper Palatinate
item.description: A 60-year-old is alleged to have shot and killed a male and a female employee of the Neumarkt District Office during a routine weapons check.

item.title: 'Fire hoses' are Britain's nuclear submarine's only defence against drone attacks, reports say
item.description: While drone attacks are becoming a major threat in armed conflicts, Britain's nuclear submarines are revealed to use "fire hoses" to defend themselves against air attacks, reports say.

item.title: Huge victory for Spain as two cities crowned greenest in the EU. Which countries missed out?
item.description: The winner of the European Green Capital 2028 awards is going home with €600,000 to help turn ambition into further action.

item.title: EU may need to cut winter gas demand by 7% as storage hits record low, IEEFA warns
item.description: The EU could have to curb gas consumption by 7% this winter, the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis warned on Friday, with stocks at their lowest for the time of year on record and the Iran war keeping prices high ahead of a full ban on Russian LNG imports from January 2027.

item.title: Latest attacks on Ukraine are ‘war crimes done by Putin’, says Ukrainian politician
item.description: Yulia Klymenko, a member of Ukraine’s parliament, says Russia “cannot achieve anything on the front line” and is therefore waging a “fight and genocide against civilians” in Ukraine, following a targeted attack that killed 33 civilians.

item.title: Cars burned and shops looted as anti-immigration protests rock South Africa
item.description: South Africa saw violent anti-immigration protests in Soweto and Durban on Thursday, 8 October, after a Constitutional Court ruling eased restrictions on asylum applications.

item.title: Chile: Santiago flooding turns streets to rivers as Kast declares state of catastrophe
item.description: Torrential rain caused severe flooding in Santiago, Chile, leaving homes, clinics and university buildings under water.

item.title: Hungary's 2026 drought is the country's most severe in 126 years, data shows
item.description: The central European nation has been facing a critical water shortage following a drought that began in the second half of 2025.

item.title: Rima Hassan denies throwing the EU flag to the floor at 7 October commemoration
item.description: French EU lawmaker Rima Hassan has denied throwing to the floor the EU flag at a 7 October commemoration, stressing she has asked for the CCTV footages to be made available to the press.

item.title: France faces perfect storm of student unrest and economic turmoil
item.description: Good morning. Mared Gwyn here with your Friday newsletter. Today: the perfect political storm that’s engulfing the French government, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s plea to his international partners.

item.title: The funniest animal photos of 2026: Nikon Comedy Wildlife Awards finalists revealed
item.description: This year’s competition attracted more than 10,000 entries from 112 countries - a record for the awards.

item.title: US sailors reunite with families as USS Abraham Lincoln returns home
item.description: Sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln reunite with their families in San Diego after a 265-day deployment supporting US military operations against Iran.

item.title: 'Modern-day Thomas Edison': Trump awards Elon Musk top US science medal
item.description: Despite the president's glowing words at the award ceremony, Trump and Musk have navigated a rather volatile relationship in recent years.

item.title: US military will livestream the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter, 'torture' for UN
item.description: Convicted military base shooter Nidal Hasan's execution will take place on 3 December at Fort Hood military base, where he committed the shooting. It will be the first US military execution carried out by a firing squad since World War II.

item.title: Europe Today: French students 'retake Bastille', Trump 'unwilling' to help Ukraine
item.description: French students have “retaken the Bastille”, says Jean-Luc Mélenchon, after a mass rally in Paris. Volodymyr Zelenskyy accuses the US of “unwillingness” to help Ukraine. And former New Zealand PM Helen Clark joins us on critical minerals as MEP Rima Hassan faces fallout over flags row.

item.title: QatarEnergy’s LNG expansion targets early 2027 production amid reports of $3bn loan
item.description: QatarEnergy is advancing its LNG expansion and has reportedly secured a $3 billion (€2.68bn) loan from Chinese banks as war damage and shipping risks constrain exports. Shipments through Hormuz are recovering, but remain far below pre-war levels.

item.title: Are eurozone bond markets warning of a recession as growth slows?
item.description: Eurostat's cycle clock, which tracks the economy's phases, flags a sharp slowdown in the eurozone. Bond markets highlight French fiscal stress, sticky inflation and ECB hikes. But that could shift soon.

item.title: Graphene opens new way to detect brain damage after stroke
item.description: An international team of scientists involving Spain's CSIC has developed graphene sensors that pinpoint the brain regions most vulnerable after a stroke, tested in mice, opening the door to preventing further damage and improving treatment.

item.title: El Niño could weaken the polar vortex. Does a scorching summer mean a freezing winter?
item.description: El Niño’s European weather impacts tend to be indirect and less severe than in the tropics. But experts warn it could weaken the polar vortex.

item.title: Russia slashes cancer care as defence spending hits post-Soviet record
item.description: The federal cancer programme budget falls from 44.9 billion to 3.87 billion roubles in 2027 — a nearly 40-fold reduction against 2025 levels — as defence spending reaches 35% of all federal expenditure, the highest share since the Soviet Union collapsed.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 9th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 9th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Santorini: Wine, gastronomy and unique experiences beyond the famous sunsets
item.description: At the October tourism forum, GNTO representatives presented the travel preferences of tourists from key European markets, and local authorities are preparing 32 short videos to highlight lesser-known aspects of the Greek island.

item.title: From barbershops to nature courses: How community-driven campaigns are rethinking men’s mental health
item.description: As waiting lists for mental health care continue to grow, community-driven campaigns across Europe have been finding unique ways to support men in particular.

item.title: Six injured as heavy rains batter Chile's capital, sweeping away cars and flooding homes
item.description: Authorities have placed 10 other Chilean districts on high alert as risks of potential mudslides and rain-related emergencies threaten to batter the region.

item.title: Police boost presence and detain 17-year-old after 'Bloody Friday' threat to Polish schools
item.description: Warnings about an alleged series of attacks on schools planned for 9 October have circulated on social media. Police say they are monitoring the situation and will deploy officers to schools they believe are at risk. In several towns in the Mazovia region, on-site classes have been cancelled.

item.title: Masked ICE officers shoot a man while making an arrest in New York, officials say
item.description: Eyewitnesses say they saw a few masked officers wearing Department of Homeland Security branded clothes surrounding a man on the ground who appeared injured. They say they heard three or four gunshots being fired.

item.title: Kyiv open to 'constructive dialogue' after Seoul recalls its ambassador amid North Korean POW disclosure row
item.description: Kyiv says it is open to “constructive dialogue” with Seoul despite its decision to recall its ambassador. South Korea’s decision comes just days after its president threatened to take punitive action against Zelenskyy’s violation of the non-disclosure agreement.

item.title: Barcelona team develops AI that detects ageing in blood stem cells
item.description: ChromAgeNet has decoded chromatin architecture, the 3D organisation of DNA in the nucleus, distinguishing young from aged blood stem cells and opening new paths for cell rejuvenation.

item.title: Deadly floods sweep Albania and Montenegro as rivers burst banks
item.description: Homes surrounded by water, flooded roads and farmland submerged beneath swollen rivers. Albania and Montenegro were still battling severe flooding on Thursday, 8 January, after days of torrential rain and heavy snow.

item.title: Hundreds of farmers rally in Paris against EU-Mercosur pact and import fears
item.description: Hundreds of French farmers drive tractors into Paris to protest the EU‑Mercosur deal, warning of unfair competition and demanding stronger protections.

item.title: US aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln returns to San Diego after record deployment
item.description: After more than 10 months at sea, the Lincoln made a stop in Thailand last month on its way back from the Middle East.

item.title: Fire rages at Yandex data centre after Ukraine drone attack
item.description: A Yandex data centre in Russia’s Ryazan region caught fire and was taken offline after what the company said was a Ukrainian drone attack.

item.title: ‘We will continue’: Madrid protesters pay tribute to 87-year-old woman
item.description: Protesters gathered in Madrid to remember 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal, whose eviction from her longtime home sparked a nationwide housing protest movement. Protesters say her death will strengthen their determination to continue the campaign.

item.title: Ex-prince Andrew warrants ruled 'unlawful' as police investigation continues
item.description: According to British media reports, it is the first time a member of the royal family has challenged the legality of criminal proceedings since the trial of Charles I in 1649.

item.title: Tsunoda Claims World Gold as Murao Retains His Title in Baku
item.description: Ai Tsunoda Roustant claimed her first senior world title at -70kg, defeating Michaela Polleres in golden score. At -90kg, Sanshiro Murao delivered a spectacular ippon against Goki Tajima in an all-Japanese final, defending his title to become a two-time world champion.

item.title: Taxes account for over 53% of labour costs in Spain, study finds
item.description: In 2025, Spain's Finance Ministry argued that its tax cuts for middle-income earners had delivered €38 billion in savings

item.title: Pro-Russian hacker group NoName targets Italian Foreign Ministry website
item.description: Checks are under way on the websites of Italian embassies and consulates abroad following a suspected similar cyberattack by pro-Russian hackers

item.title: EU debates harsh working conditions for fishers: 'I had no other choice'
item.description: Endless weeks, shifts of up to 24 hours and even no drinking water: these were some of the hardships aired last week at a debate held by the EU Fisheries Committee with sector representatives.

item.title: Mélenchon declares ‘Bastille retaken’ after major student rally in Paris
item.description: The mass student-led movement emerged over a range of issues including long school days, overcrowded schools, teacher absences.

item.title: Drought: groundwater levels in France remain very low
item.description: France's groundwater levels remain deeply worrying at the start of October: two-thirds of monitoring sites are below normal and 81% are still falling. The autumn recharge, vital to rebuild reserves, has yet to get under way.

item.title: Astronaut Sophie Adenot returns to Earth after record space mission
item.description: Sophie Adenot left the International Space Station on Wednesday after an eight-month stay, the longest by a European astronaut, and splashed down on Thursday at around 5.30 pm with three fellow crew members.

item.title: Italy probes gaming giant Activision Blizzard over in-game spending by children
item.description: Italy’s antitrust authority is investigating whether monetisation practices in Call of Duty Mobile and Diablo Immortal amount to a “widespread infringement” of EU consumer protection rules, particularly in relation to children.

item.title: US charges former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro with torture
item.description: The revised indictment includes several mentions of the involvement of Venezuela’s feared DGCIM military intelligence agency

item.title: Tiny turtles take their first steps towards the sea
item.description: On Mataking Island in Malaysia, conservationists raise and release green turtle hatchlings, part of long-running efforts that helped the species recover.
